## [0.7.4] - 2026-09-30

### Added

- The Security settings page now has an **Operator "Keep me signed in" duration (days)** field (0 to 14, 3 by default), so a superadmin can change how long a remembered operator session lasts, or set 0 to hide the sign-in checkbox, without editing environment variables. It is read-only when `OPERATOR_REMEMBER_ME_DAYS` is set.
- Operators can now tick **Keep me signed in** on the sign-in page, so a check-in tablet stays signed in between shifts instead of asking for the password again after two hours of inactivity or twelve hours in total. A remembered session lasts 3 days by default (`operator_remember_me_days` in system settings or `OPERATOR_REMEMBER_ME_DAYS`, 0 to 14; 0 hides the checkbox), and the session cookie is kept when the browser or tablet app is closed. It applies to operator accounts only: administrators and superadministrators keep their 12 hour limit and 30 minute inactivity timeout even if they tick the box. Signing out still ends the session immediately, and a remembered session can be revoked from Active sessions like any other. It applies to password sign-in only; passkey and SSO sign-in are unchanged. Includes a database migration (one new column on sessions), applied by the usual migration step.
- Event cards now keep the last forecast after the event is over, shown as **Last forecast** (for example 18°C) with the weather provider's credit. Weather providers cannot look back, so Admitto now saves the latest forecast it sees for an event's day whenever someone opens the Events list, the event, or the check-in event list while the day is still ahead, and shows that one afterwards. Events that ended before this release, or whose day nobody had a list open for in the days before, have none and show no weather chip. Moving an event to another day or place discards its saved forecast. Includes a database migration (one new nullable column on events), applied by the usual migration step.
- Check-in progress on Overview now shows **Wallet passes installed** (for example 268, 65%) for events that use wallets, next to Last check-in. It counts attendees whose pass was confirmed on a device at any point, the same way the Wallets report does, so it does not drop when someone removes a pass.
- Attendees → **More actions** has a new **Void active passes** action that makes every active wallet pass of the event show as invalid, in the background, instead of being limited to 100 selected attendees. It asks for confirmation, shows a short summary when it is done (voided, left alone, could not be voided), and can be run again to retry the passes that failed. It works on an archived event and with the Wallet switch off, like **Void wallet pass**. The worker picks it up as a new `wallet_cleanup` job, and one new database migration keeps at most one such job per event.
- Attendees → **More actions** has a new **Remove inactive passes** action that removes every voided or expired wallet pass of the event from the wallet service, once it has stayed inactive for at least a day (voided or expired for a day, counted from whichever applies), in the background - instead of being limited to 100 selected attendees. It keeps each pass's local record and its history in Reports, the same as **Remove from provider** on one attendee, and shows a short summary when it is done. It works on an archived event and with the Wallet switch off. The Archive event dialog now also names how many inactive wallet passes are still at the wallet service, since archiving does not remove them. One new database migration keeps at most one such job per event.
- The Health check tab now shows a one-sentence verdict above the check groups (for example "No problems found." or "1 check is down and 2 are degraded."), coloured by whether anything is down or degraded. Group titles (Core infrastructure, External integrations) are now proper headings instead of unlabelled text.
- Event Settings → Wallet has a new **Pass expiration** field: **Do not expire automatically** (unchanged default) or **Expire when the event ends**, which gives every issued or reissued pass a real expiration date matching the event's own end time and sends it to the wallet provider. Turning it on requires **Test connection** to first confirm the template supports a per-pass expiration date; turning it back off is blocked once any pass has been issued, since there is no confirmed way to clear an already-sent date. Turning it on, or later rescheduling the event while it is on, now also reaches a voided pass's own expiration, not only active ones. A pass whose own expiration date has passed now goes **Expired** automatically, checked independently of the wallet provider and of whether the event is archived, and can no longer be restored, the same as one whose event is already over. Includes a database migration (new columns on events and wallet passes, plus an index for the expiry check), applied by the usual migration step.
- Health check's known down or degraded states (the database, rate limits, the background worker, the mail queue, sending mail, identity providers, and Cloudflare Access) now show one sentence on what it affects and one on what to do next when the row is expanded, above its own details, with a link to the relevant settings tab where one helps. A state this list does not cover still shows only its details, as before.
- Health check's guidance now also covers file storage, address lookup, weather, and bounce detection. Email sending shows a quieter, non-alarming note instead when no organisation mail provider is set, or the set provider only exports rather than sends, each pointing to Mail settings; this note does not change the tab's verdict, since a not configured row already does not count toward it.

### Changed

- The workflows that mint a token from the release GitHub App now pass its Client ID (`client-id`) instead of the deprecated numeric App ID (`app-id`), which removes a deprecation warning from every release, wiki and Scorecard run. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- The automated pull request review now reads the pull request description as the author's notes, and no longer blocks a change only because it depends on a repository secret, setting or branch rule it cannot see: if the description says it is in place it accepts that, and if not it lists the dependency for the maintainer to confirm. A defect it can see in the code still blocks. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- A pull request that changes only documentation (Markdown files under `docs/`, and `CHANGELOG.md`) is now approved by a path rule without running the AI review, and the approval says so. Anything else in the change, including `.github/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or a renamed source file, makes it an ordinary change that gets the full review. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- The automated pull request review now runs on the maintainer's Claude subscription instead of per-token API billing, stops after 6 automated review attempts on one pull request or 80 in a day, counting failed attempts too (a manual re-run of the job bypasses this), and posts a plain comment, without approving, when it cannot run because a limit was reached or the service failed. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- The **AI review backtest** workflow now takes an optional reasoning effort (`low` to `xhigh`) for the reviewer, so how deep it thinks can be measured against its cost on past changes. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- A new manual workflow, **AI review backtest**, runs the automated pull request review against past changes whose real defects are already known and prints what it would have said, without posting anything, so a change to the reviewer's prompt can be measured before it goes live. The backtest reads its copy of the reviewer's prompt, output schema and diff builder from `.github/ai-review/`. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- The automated pull request review now waits one minute after the last push before it starts (and not at all when it is re-run by hand), so a quick series of pushes costs one review instead of one per push. It also leaves lockfiles out of what the reviewer reads (they are named at the top of its input), never approves when a changed file's diff is unavailable, and shows its cost in the job summary. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- Pull requests from the maintainer now get an automated review from a second identity (`github-actions[bot]`), which approves when it finds no blocking problem and otherwise comments. It only reviews: it never merges, so merging stays a manual decision, and the required checks still apply. The review runs from the `main` version of the workflow, reads only the diff with read-only tools, skips Dependabot and fork PRs, and is not posted if the text looks like it contains a credential. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- CI no longer keeps a committed ESLint warning baseline. Every rule that had been left at a warning is now an error, so `npm run lint` runs with `--max-warnings 0` and any warning fails it directly; the baseline file, its check script, its tests, and the CI step and Sonar entries that pointed at them are removed. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- The last ESLint security-rule warnings are cleared and `detect-unsafe-regex` is now enforced as an error, so the tracked warning baseline is empty. Five patterns (the mail-settings domain label check, the Redis loopback check, the house-number pattern, and the two time-zone offset readers) were rewritten without a nested quantifier and accept exactly the same text, checked on millions of generated inputs; three patterns that are linear but have a shape the rule dislikes (the notification e-mail check, the trailing-number split of a street segment, and the upload-path finder) keep a narrow suppression that says why. Behaviour is unchanged, and new tests pin the house-number, loopback, domain-label, time-zone offset and hostile-input cases.
- The bounce-mail parser's pattern helper now accepts only the parser's own build-time fragments, so interpolating any other value into a pattern is a type error instead of a promise in a comment. All nine patterns are byte-identical to before, so bounce parsing behaves exactly as it did. A lint configuration comment that miscounted the remaining audited string-built patterns was corrected, and one test now really proves that an indented continuation line stays in the same delivery-status block.
- Bounce-mail parsing now builds all of its patterns through one audited helper that only ever receives the parser's own constant fragments, and two patterns (the blank-line splitter for delivery-status blocks and the HTML tag stripper) were rewritten without nested quantifiers. Matching is identical, checked against several million generated inputs, and the delivery-status splitter and the HTML tag stripper now handle very long or malformed bounce bodies in milliseconds. The `detect-non-literal-regexp` security lint rule is now enforced as an error, so a new string-built pattern has to be justified.
- The wallet confirmation dialogs and menu hints (Void, Restore, Push updates, Refresh status, Delete wallet pass, Remove from provider) now use plainer words. "Irreversible", "provider" and "left untouched" are gone from the explanations: they now say what the action does, what stays (the pass on the phone, check-in, the history in Reports), and how it differs from Remove and Delete.
- The **Add to Wallet** buttons on an attendee's ticket page now close when they can no longer work. They disappear once the event is over or archived, and for an attendee whose wallet pass is voided, expired or removed at the provider, and an older link to a button simply returns to the ticket without an error. Before, an expired or removed pass showed a "could not add" message, and tapping the link for a voided pass quietly restored it at the provider. Now only **Restore wallet pass** on Attendee Detail brings a voided pass back, and it is refused once the event is over: it is no longer offered there, and restoring an attendee's ticket after the event no longer restores their wallet pass. An event is over at its end time in its own time zone, or at the end of its day when it has none; an event that ends after midnight ends on the next day.
- Lookups by a stored or computed name in the Wallet pass mapper, notification settings, address components, bounce-mail parsing, and the auth settings resolver no longer index plain objects with that name, and the `detect-object-injection` security lint rule is now enforced as an error for the server packages. Two edge cases are corrected as a side effect: a Wallet field mapping whose placeholder is named like a built-in property (for example `constructor`) no longer puts that built-in into the pass data, and the Wallet push relevance check now treats an unknown field name that happens to match a built-in property as relevant instead of failing. A stored `__proto__` key in a Wallet mapping or in notification settings was already ignored and stays ignored.
- The attendee PDF export's column layout and the readers for a ticket's stored address and Wallet field mapping no longer look values up by a computed key, which clears 18 findings of the `detect-object-injection` security lint rule in `@admitto/tickets`. PDF exports, ticket pages, and Wallet passes come out exactly the same; the only difference is that a stored Wallet mapping key named `__proto__`, which was already dropped by accident, is now skipped explicitly.
- The rest of the Admin SPA's buttons, forms, and navigation links that start an asynchronous action (identity provider editors, Attendees export, check-in lookup, session and security panels, and similar) now explicitly mark their intentionally unawaited work, and the ESLint rule that guards this (`no-misused-promises`) is now enforced as an error, so a future async handler that could silently drop its failure is caught during development. Every one of these actions already showed its own error, retry state, or toast, so nothing changes for administrators or operators.
- The Overview page of an archived event now shows an amber notice explaining what archiving means, with a **Restore event** button for superadmins, instead of fixed text in the corner and under the subtitle. Restoring asks for confirmation first and takes effect straight away, so there is no need to open Event settings. Other roles see a short note to ask a superadmin.
- My Account's confirm dialogs, password form, profile save, and passkey or security key step-up button now explicitly mark their intentionally unawaited work, so a future async handler that could silently drop its failure is caught during development. Each of these actions already showed its own error, so nothing changes for administrators.
- Admitto now notices when PassCreator has voided or expired a wallet pass on its own. The background wallet sync and **Refresh status** read the pass again and, when PassCreator reports it voided or expired, mark it **Voided** here too, so it stops looking active and offers the voided actions (Restore, Delete). Until a PassCreator time zone setting arrives in a following release, an expired pass is shown as voided rather than expired. The background wallet sync and **Refresh status** only read active passes from now on (the background sync also leaves archived events alone): a voided or expired pass keeps the last registration counts it had and is no longer polled, which also saves PassCreator API calls, and **Refresh status** is no longer offered for one. Includes a database migration (one new column on wallet passes), applied by the usual migration step.
- PassCreator's voided notification is now treated as a signal to read the pass again instead of being taken at face value. A late redelivery can no longer void a pass that was restored in the meantime, and if the read fails the notification is answered with an error so PassCreator sends it again. After a **Void** or **Restore** made in Admitto, a stale answer from PassCreator within the next ten minutes is ignored rather than undoing it, and when two reads of the same pass overlap, the older one can no longer overwrite the newer one. PassCreator's notifications are also still processed while the event's Wallet switch is off, so a pass voided then is not missed.
- **Void wallet pass**, **Delete wallet pass**, **Refresh status** and the new **Remove from provider** (below) now work on an archived event and when the event's Wallet switch is off, on Attendee Detail and in the Attendees list's bulk menu, so passes can be wound down after an event has ended without reopening it. **Push updates** and **Restore wallet pass** stay disabled there as before.
- Attendee Detail and the Attendees list's bulk menu now offer **Remove from provider** for a voided or expired wallet pass: it permanently deletes the pass at the wallet provider while keeping the attendee's local record and its Reports history (installs, registrations) - unlike **Delete wallet pass**, which erases both. This is what actually stops the provider counting a pass against its own registration plan once it is no longer valid; **Void** alone does not. A removed pass shows a **Removed from provider** date on the attendee's Wallet card and in the Wallets CSV export, and its registration counts on the Attendees list are now labelled "Was registered" instead of "Registered" to make clear they are a frozen last-known snapshot, not a live read. Includes a database migration (two new columns on wallet passes and a rebuilt index for the wallet sync), applied by the usual migration step.
- An expired wallet pass now offers only **Delete wallet pass** and **Remove from provider** on Attendee Detail - expiry is permanent, so there is no Restore, Push updates, or Refresh status for it. Reopening an old "Add to Wallet" link for an expired pass no longer silently marks it active again without actually restoring anything at the provider; the link simply returns to the ticket (see the Add to Wallet bullet above).
- Check-in live updates are now more tolerant of reconnects. On phones, unstable Wi-Fi or mobile data, or behind a reverse proxy, the live stream can drop and reconnect many times a minute, and operators quickly saw "Live updates paused briefly (too many reconnects)". The default request limits are raised from 12 to 120 per minute for one operator and event, and from 48 to 240 per minute for one operator across all events. The limit on how many streams one operator can keep open at once is unchanged (3 per event, 12 in total).
- The check-in live update limits can now be changed with environment variables, without a new release or image: `CHECKIN_STREAM_RATE_LIMIT_PER_EVENT`, `CHECKIN_STREAM_RATE_LIMIT_PER_ACTOR`, `CHECKIN_STREAM_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `CHECKIN_STREAM_MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_EVENT` and `CHECKIN_STREAM_MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_ACTOR`. Recreate the container after changing them (for example `docker compose up -d`; a plain restart does not re-read `.env`). A value that is not a positive whole number is ignored, the default is used, and a warning is logged at startup. See `deploy/ENV.md`.
- The Overview cards now line up. Each row of cards has one height, Recent activity scrolls inside the height of Check-in progress instead of using a fixed height of its own, and what is inside a card keeps its normal size at the top instead of being stretched, so short cards end with a single quiet blank strip rather than gaps between items. Setup checklist rows are also a little more compact.
- Check-in progress on Overview is simpler: the ring now sits beside one large checked-in number, with the rest shown as **not yet arrived**, or as **no-shows** once the event is over (after its end time when one is set, otherwise at the end of its day). The ticket-type breakdown and the repeated legend are gone (ticket types are in Reports), and Busiest hour appears only when the event does not use wallets.
- The Overview **Setup checklist** now shows a progress bar (green, amber, or red depending on the worst check), lists problems before completed checks, and every row links to the page that fixes it. The link to Event settings at the bottom is gone.
- Bringing an archived event back is now called **Restore** everywhere, matching the button on the Overview: the **Restore event** button and the **Restore this event?** dialog in Event settings, the **Restore** button and dialog in the Archiving list, the **Event restored.** message, and the **Event restored** entry in the audit log (older entries show the new name too). What it does is unchanged.
- Event hours on the public ticket page, in emails, and on wallet passes now show a numeric time zone offset as UTC+2 instead of GMT+2, matching the admin, which already wrote it that way. Named abbreviations such as CET and EDT are unchanged, and so is GMT itself for zones that really use it (UK winter time). A wallet pass that was already added keeps its old text until it is next updated.
- On Organisation settings, Health check now shows the "Generated" time, version, and commit on its own line directly under the tab description, so it wraps like normal text on narrow screens instead of sharing a row with the description. The "Run live checks" tooltip and its More actions hint now say the same thing and list every test a live run adds, including weather and writing to the upload folder.
- The Wallets report's **Wallet lifecycle** card is now three separate cards - **Pass validity** (active, voided, or expired), **Provider state** (still at the wallet service, or removed from it), and **Registration state (last known)** (registered, previously registered, or never installed) - since a pass can be voided while still registered, or removed from the provider while still showing as registered, and one card could not show that. The PDF export gained matching sections. Communication's **By wallet status** filter, which reads the same registration data, now says "Registered (last known)", "Previously registered (last known)", and "Never installed" to match.
- Health check rows now show a status circle with a glyph (a check, triangle, cross or dash) plus a Down, Degraded or Not configured badge next to the label, instead of relying on a small coloured dot and the row's border colour alone. A healthy row shows no badge. The summary text stays the same muted colour on every row; only the circle, badge and border now carry the colour.
- Health check rows within a group now sort with problems first (Down, then Degraded, then healthy, then Not configured), and a Down or Degraded row opens automatically to show its detail. Manually expanding or collapsing a row is remembered as long as its status stays the same; it is forgotten once a later report (including a live run) shows a different status for that row, so a row collapsed while degraded re-opens if it later goes down. Exporting a snapshot keeps the original order.
- A Health check row's expanded detail list is easier to read: labels are sentence-case instead of every word capitalised, technical codes like `reason` and `live_check` show as short plain phrases, `stale_after_ms` shows in minutes, yes/no values are capitalised, and a detail already repeated in the row's own summary (for example a degraded row's latency) is no longer shown twice. The Background worker row also gains a **Last seen** fact next to its label once its heartbeat is a minute or older, measured against the report's own Generated time so it never counts up on its own; the export and the Markdown snapshot are unchanged.
- The checks on pull requests now have readable names instead of internal ids, for example **Wiki docs - sync and links** instead of `wiki-docs` and **Database migration safety** instead of `migration-safety`, so it is clear at a glance what each check verifies. What each check verifies has not changed.
- The pull request check that scans for real personal data, previously shown as just `scan`, is now named **Privacy guard - no real personal data in PR**. What it verifies has not changed.
- Event settings → Danger zone no longer shows a disabled **Revoke all Wallet passes** placeholder. The action it was reserving space for now exists, as **Void active passes** and **Remove inactive passes** under Attendees → More actions, kept there rather than duplicated into Danger zone so wallet lifecycle management stays in one place.
- The automated pull request review now reads its prompt, output schema and diff rules from `.github/ai-review/`, the same files its backtest measures, so a backtest of the `live` variant tests exactly what runs, and a test keeps them from drifting apart again. Its spend limits now also count a run that a newer push cancelled once it had got past the one-minute wait, when the reviewer may already have started, which used to escape both the per-PR and the daily limit. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.

### Security

- The bounce reader is no longer slow on a bounce message with a very long run of spaces or tabs inside a reason. One crafted message of about 64 KB sent to a bounce mailbox could keep the worker busy for around three seconds (and the web app, when an admin ran bounce detection by hand), so a few of them could stall mail sending and other background jobs. Runs of blanks are now collapsed before matching, and every supported mail-server format has a test for it.
- Release SBOMs are now attached to the GitHub Release first and signed afterwards, so a Sigstore or attestation outage can no longer leave a release without them (the run still fails visibly, and the **Sign release assets** workflow can add the signatures later). The release tag is also now created on the exact commit whose CI passed, so a change merged while the release waits for CI cannot end up inside it. Attaching the SBOMs also no longer fails when the release workflow creates the GitHub Release at the same moment. SECURITY.md now explains how to verify a release's SBOM signature and image provenance, and that an SBOM without a signature next to it has not been verified.
- A new manual workflow, **Sign release assets**, attaches a Sigstore signature to the SBOMs of releases published before signing existed (v0.7.0 to v0.7.3), so they can be verified with `cosign verify-blob` too. It signs only; it does not add build provenance to files it did not build. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- Every release now attaches a Sigstore signature (`.sigstore.json`) for each SBOM and a signed provenance file (`provenance-<tag>.intoto.jsonl`), so the release assets can be verified with `cosign verify-blob` or `gh attestation verify`, not only the container image. The OpenSSF Scorecard workflow now reads the branch rules with a short-lived read-only token from the release GitHub App, so its Branch-Protection check no longer errors out. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- Published container images now carry a BuildKit SBOM attestation next to the existing provenance attestation, so tools such as Docker Scout can read the package list straight from the image. The CycloneDX SBOM on each GitHub Release is unchanged.
- The Health check "Copy for GitHub Issue" and Export snapshots no longer include an identity provider's display name, a map tile server's address, or the database's exact patch version. Identity providers now show as **Identity provider, OIDC** (or SAML) and map tiles as **Map tiles** in the snapshot, and the database engine shows its major version only (for example PostgreSQL 16). The Health check tab itself is unchanged and still shows the exact values.
- On Organisation settings, Health check, an unexpected connection error on the Weather row's live check no longer shows its exact message anywhere; the row shows a general reason instead. An unrecognized file storage provider no longer appears in the row's summary text or in the Export and Copy for GitHub Issue snapshots; the Health check tab itself still shows the value you set, so you can see what needs fixing.

### Fixed

- Key contacts on Overview now check what you enter. The phone field no longer accepts letters (typing or pasting keeps only digits and the usual separators), a number must have 3 to 15 digits, and an email must be a valid address, with the message shown under the field before you can save. The server applies the same checks, so a bad value cannot be saved by other means, and the Call and Email buttons now build their links from safe forms of the stored value. A contact saved earlier with an old-style phone or email can still be edited as long as you do not change that field.
- Editing an attendee whose wallet pass was already removed from the provider, while revoking them in the same save, no longer sends a pointless update request to the provider for a pass that no longer exists there. The pass stays as it was.
- Switching to another event while a save or restore was still finishing could leave the previous event's details in the sidebar and pages under the new event's address until the page was reloaded. The late answer is now ignored once you have moved to a different event.
- The event countdown tile on Overview no longer cuts "Ended 4 days ago" short with an ellipsis. An event that ended within the past week now reads **4 days ago** (or **Yesterday**, **Today**) under the label **Event ended**, at the same size as the other three numbers on the row.
- Zooming or panning the map on the event's Location tab no longer changes the map shown in tickets, emails, and event cards. Before, every zoom step there was saved as the event's map zoom, so exploring the surroundings (or zooming in to place the pin precisely) silently changed those images and marked the tab as having unsaved changes. Those maps stay at the default zoom, centred on the pin, and a new pin placement or venue search resets to that default. An event that already saved a different zoom before this release keeps it until its pin is placed again or its venue is searched again.
- Security notification emails now show readable context instead of internal identifiers. For example, an administrator-role alert names the person who made the change and the person receiving the role in the message, then shows **Role: Administrator** and **Scope: Organisation name**; it never exposes `actor_user_id`, `target_user_id`, or `scope_id`. The other alerts likewise use reader-facing labels for failed-attempt counts, emergency actions, sign-in location/device/time, and identity-provider changes. Future notification types show no email details until their human-facing labels are defined.
- The published image's `org.opencontainers.image.revision` label and the commit shown in the admin build info could name a later commit than the one the image was built from when a release was republished by hand, as happened for 0.7.3, which reported `8d64005` instead of the tagged `68e3f79`. The release build now stamps the commit it actually checked out and fails if the image label disagrees. Images published before 0.7.4 keep their original label.
- The Reports admission log now lists the newest admission first instead of the oldest, and the CSV and printable PDF exports follow the same order. Before, an event with more than 500 admissions (100 in the PDF) showed only its earliest check-ins, so the most recent ones were missing from the table; it now shows the latest ones and says so in the truncation note.
- On phones and tablets, tapping the scan field on the check-in page now opens the on-screen keyboard, so an operator can type a name or email when a QR code will not scan. Before, the field was set up for hardware scanners and told the device never to show a keyboard, which left touch-only devices with no way to type into it. Desktop computers and other devices without a touchscreen behave as before.
- Event cards no longer show a false "Weather unavailable" error once the event is over. Before, every event whose day had passed showed a cloud-off chip saying the forecast could not be loaded and pointing to External services, even though the weather provider worked fine, because weather providers only serve today and the days ahead. Weather for events that are still ahead, and the public ticket page, are unchanged.
- The event-wide **Push updates** and **Refresh status** confirmations on the Attendees page no longer carry over to another event. Before, a confirmation left open on one event stayed on screen after you switched to a different event, and confirming it there queued the job for that other event instead of the one you had opened it on. For **Push updates** that meant sending new content to every installed wallet pass of an event you had not confirmed. The confirmation now closes when you switch events, and confirming only ever acts on the event it was opened on.
- The event-wide **Void active passes** confirmation on the Attendees page could reappear on its own after you switched away from an event and back to it, and confirming it then genuinely voided every active wallet pass of that event without you opening the confirmation again. The confirmation now follows the same rule as **Push updates** and **Refresh status**: it closes when you switch events and stays closed until you open it again.
- On Organisation settings, Health check, a row that is down now gets the red border it was meant to have. Before, only its dot was red while a degraded row got a full amber border, because a few style names in the tab's stylesheet did not exist. Background worker and Bounce detection also get their own icons instead of a plain dot.
- On Organisation settings, Health check, the Instance URL row (when BASE_URL is only optional, in development) and the File storage row (before the upload folder has been created) now show as **Not configured** instead of **Degraded**. Neither is a real problem, so a fresh development install no longer shows an amber warning on an otherwise healthy instance. **Run live checks** now also creates a missing upload folder and then reports File storage as Connected, or as Down with "Cannot create the upload folder" when it cannot. An instance whose address is saved only in Settings (no `BASE_URL` set) now shows the Instance URL row as **Degraded** ("BASE_URL not set") with a hint, instead of **Down**, and a detail such as "Configured: No" is no longer hidden just because the row's summary contains the same letters ("Not configured"). When the row is Down, its hint now says to correct or remove an invalid `BASE_URL` first, because it is read before the address saved in General settings.
- On a multi-instance deployment, a wallet pass that one instance had just issued successfully could be overwritten back to failed by a second, slower instance racing the same attendee's first "Add to Wallet" tap, if that second instance's own duplicate check happened to miss the pass the first one had already created. The pass on the phone was never affected, only its local record; that record is now left alone once it already shows the pass as issued.
- The Setup checklist's fix-it text for a failing database check no longer says migrations run automatically when the app container starts; in Docker Compose they run once, before the app starts, in the separate `migrate` service. The Instance URL fix-it text, and the row's own status line above it, no longer offer Settings → General as an equal alternative to BASE_URL, and no longer say this is enforced at boot: Admitto already works with only the Settings value set, but this specific check wants BASE_URL and stays red without it.
- The topbar **System status** menu could show "All systems normal" for a superadmin while the Health check tab showed the background worker down or degraded, since the topbar never looked at the worker at all. It now shows a **Background worker** row alongside Database, Session storage and Data encryption, reading the same heartbeat as the Health check tab, and factors it into the trigger's own state (as Degraded, never as the harder Action needed, since a stalled worker only delays mail delivery, import/export and bounce detection rather than breaking the app).
- A wallet pass is now marked **Expired** only once its event's current end time has passed too. If the event's end time was moved later and the new expiration date had not reached a pass yet (for example because a second edit was saved while the first update was still running), the pass used to turn Expired in the middle of the event and could not be restored. The worker now leaves such passes alone until the event is really over, and it checks that under a lock on the event, so an end time moved later at that very moment cannot slip through.
- Changing the wallet Template ID or API key while **Pass expiration** is set to **Expire when the event ends** now checks again that the new template supports a per-pass expiration date, and refuses the save when it does not. Before, only turning the option on was checked, so a template swap could leave every new pass without an expiration date at the wallet provider while Admitto still marked it Expired.
- The Organisation settings Health check tab now reads the report again when you come back to it, so after following a hint to another settings tab and fixing the problem there, the verdict and hints are up to date. The previous report stays on screen while the new one loads.
- The event countdown tile on Overview no longer says **Event ended** on the event's own day while the event is still going. It used to switch in the afternoon, when the Check-in card beside it still counted people who had not arrived yet; both now go by the event's end time (or the end of the day when none is set). An overnight event, for example 22:00 to 02:00, no longer reads as ended between midnight and its end time either.
- The bounce banner on the Communication page no longer promises that bounced addresses "will not receive future mail", which Admitto does not enforce. It now asks you to check those addresses before sending again.
- The Wallets report no longer lists a permanent **Failed (unexpected)** row with 0 in its Pass validity card and PDF. That bucket only exists to keep the card adding up to Issued and should never be above 0, so it now appears only when it is.
- The Archive event and Restore event confirmations now say the same thing on Overview, Event settings and Settings → Archiving. The Archiving panel used to describe archiving as only "hidden and read-only", without saying that check-in stops too.
- A pull request that only renames a file no longer makes the automated review treat that file as unreviewable, which had kept a documentation-only move from ever being approved. Nothing changes for operators or attendees.
- The vulnerability scan and SBOM of a published release image now use the platform that was actually built, instead of whichever platform Trivy resolved from the image digest. That mix-up made the v0.7.3 tag-push publish fail and let the arm64 gate look at the wrong image.
- Long **More actions** menus (such as the Attendees bulk actions) no longer lose the dividers between their groups, and no longer flash out past the edge of their button for a moment when they open.

---

### Deploy
- Container image: `ghcr.io/solarssk/admitto:0.7.4` (rolling `:0.7`)
- Migrations apply **automatically on container start**. **No manual `migrate deploy`.** Back up the database yourself before upgrading (the stack no longer takes an automatic pre-migration backup).

[Full changelog](https://github.com/solarssk/admitto/blob/v0.7.4/CHANGELOG.md)
